utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what you're talking about there is the extreme speeches that Brdjanin made in the media; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much like the other politicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But you picked him and Vukic and described it as the two of them, and you don't know who else, who wanted to show themselves on TV and radio. That's what you were talking about, even if other politicians were also saying awful, horrible, racist, extreme things.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you asked me about the two of them. Well, now that you're asking me about the others of other nationalities, they also did the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll take your word on that. I'm only asking you - let's move on from this. You can confirm to me, can't you, that Mr. Brdjanin made those types of speeches in the media?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were then asked: "Those sorts of words would put fear into the minds of Muslims or Croats who were listening to them, wouldn't they?" And your answer was: "Of course."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then you were asked whether the point of this, of these speeches, was to frighten Muslims and Croats into leaving, and you said: "Well, I don't know whether that was the idea, but certainly they were afraid." So again, you're confirming that these speeches frightened the Bosniak and Croat populations.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were then asked: "Isn't it true that Serbs who committed crimes against Muslims and Croats were encouraged by the comments that were made by Radoslav Brdjanin and other SDS leaders against Muslims and Croats?" And you gave a fairly detailed, articulate answer. You said: "First, my thing or first opinion that I have is that the perpetrators of crimes, where crimes were committed -- and we know in which municipalities it was even more obvious or it happened -- mostly those perpetrators must have been people who were inclined to commit such crimes. And they would always ask for certain -- some justification for the things they carried out, they committed, justification from someone else. So which means that such comments were quite useful for them, were welcome." Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So these speeches didn't just frighten people; they gave justification to the very criminals that these non-Serbs were afraid of.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you just said that they were welcome because they were a justification to the persons committing the crimes; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Justification, but the speeches were not intended for them to do such things. Well, this was being made use of by criminals of all kinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Exactly. It was being made use of. And you don't know exactly what intent Mr. Brdjanin had in his mind when he made a speech saying that only a thousand Muslims could remain and they would be old and have to clean the streets, do you? You said in your answer: "Well, you couldn't follow their minds."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, can I bring a correction in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Page 53, line 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: He says, and the transcript reflects "well, this was being made use of by criminals of all kinds." And I'm told that he added: "In the whole of BiH." So if the Court would want to confirm that with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, do you remember that which Mr. Cunningham just remarked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm now going to talk about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask, who is supplying the Defence with these corrections? Is it the accused or is it the assistant - I'm sorry, I forget your name, sir - who speaks?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It's not Mr. Brdjanin because Mr. Brdjanin doesn't hand me anything during trial. It's obviously Mr. Vujic who is watching the transcript and listening to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not obvious, I'm sorry. Because I've seen -- and there's nothing wrong with it -- But I've seen Mr. Brdjanin pass notes to you through the security guard to Mr. Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has every right to pass notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I agree with that, that he has every right to pass notes, but it's not true that he never does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question was whether it was suggested to the witness that in addition to what we have in the transcript, there was something else that he had stated, and he confirmed that he had stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I know. I'm just trying to know where it comes rom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, Judge Janu who understands the language a little bit confirms it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I wasn't doubting the accuracy of the correction, just where it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's avoid further incidents in the future. Let's move ahead, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P421, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you say P421?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, P2421.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It should be P2421. It's again wrong -- it's corrected now. Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I have some of these in the witness's language; some I don't. I'm trying to put them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, take a moment to look at that. You've seen this document before, haven't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, this is a decision of the presidency signed by Dr. Plavsic and Dr. Koljevic, 12th of May -- excuse me, 15th of April, 1992 a decision stating that a state of imminent threat of war is hereby declared; and two, the mobilisation of the TO in the whole territory of Serbian BH is hereby ordered. All right? Perhaps you haven't seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I show you P153, please. While they're getting that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's in his notebook that I prepared in the grey binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- does the tab say 153?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It should just say 153 on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this is - thank you, you talked about this yesterday - this is the decision by National Defence Minister Subotic of the 16th of April. You've seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It is addressed to the governments of the autonomous region and the SAO Serbian autonomous districts of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to all Serbian municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This refers, does it not, to the decision the day earlier we just talked about declaring an imminent threat of war? Take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if you could go to section 2, the explanation, first part states: "Municipal TOs which have functioned well up to now will continue in their existing formation and composition," and that it is intended to establish TO staffs or that TO staffs should be established in newly established Serbian municipalities along the same lines; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Number 2, "setting up of the district staffs and districts, that is placed under the jurisdiction of the Government of the SAOs, including the Autonomous Region of Krajina"; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Number 3, "the declaration of a state of imminent threat of war shall entail the taking of all necessary measures appropriate to the situation and in accordance with the specific situation in any given territory."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's recognising, isn't it, that in different areas and different circumstances, different action may be needed to be taken to accomplish what's set forth in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look at the last line above Mr. Subotic's signature, it states, and this is within the context of the general mobilisation: "In the preparations for training and deployment of the TO units, effect cooperation with the JNA units and, where possible, establish unified command."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a question and then you can comment. You can answer it. This is four days after -- well, this is in a time of great turbulence in the Krajina region; correct? It's before the establishment of the VRS, 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16th of April. It was the 12th of May, the date that the VRS was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. What I'm saying is this is earlier, it's before the establishment of the VRS. It's a time of uncertainty, problems, in the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relatively speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me take you to P1182.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the witness be allowed to make the comment that Mr. Nicholls said he could answer -- he could make after he answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I thought he did answer my question, that it was in his words a relative time of turbulence and problems. And I think from your side we've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's not what I'm talking about. I'm talking about at page 57, line 11, in the context of your asking about the final line in the general mobilisation order, he says "if I may." You then say, "Let me ask you a question. Then you can comment." I don't think he ever got the chance to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham is right, because you interrupted him just at the moment when he was going to tell us something else regarding the previous question, that is the part which established that wherever possible, there should be cooperation with JNA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we should give him the opportunity to give us any further comment that he might have or he may have on the matter. Would you like to add something to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I listened to the way you read the decision, and I answered yes, that's what it says. Item 3 -- item 2 rather, on the establishment of district staffs, placing them under the jurisdiction of the SAO Government, according to the principle information of previous district staffs, the same applies to the ARK of Bosanska Krajina, I must comment on this. This applied to district staffs, zone staffs of the Territorial Defence, and this never began to function. This never began to operate. That's one thing I would like to point out in connection with this, in order for me to comment on this decision. But this decision was never put into effect. The district staffs were never under the control of the ARK. It's a very essential distinction, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it talks about setting up of district staffs. There was a district Banja Luka TO staff at this time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not under the control of the ARK. And the military never submitted to the control of the authorities at this level. This changes the gist of the whole matter. Yes, this had been envisaged for the Territorial Defence to take over, for this to be the Army of Republika Srpska. But later on, the Army of Republika Srpska was established along the lines of the principle of the supreme staff, Main Staff, with Mladic, and that's the meeting that I talked about. My intention was to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. We're going to talk more about the TO and the topic you talked about yesterday, the changeover into light brigades which is when they became, formally, completely integrated into the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And we will talk later as well about what influence municipalities may have had over their local TOs. Now, let's about to P1182. This is almost -- this is the same document you looked at earlier. I can't remember what the exhibit number is. This is a corrected version of P167.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The correction, I believe, Your Honours, is this one correctly states "regional secretariat for National Defence" in the heading, rather than "Republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this is your order that you have based on the Subotic order we have just talked about.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is passed down to the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what you were talking about when you said you were a link yesterday, partly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The first line states that: "Pursuant to the decision of the Ministry of National Defence" - P153 that we were jus looking at of 16th of April - "and an assessment of the situation on the ground, the following decision is being set forth..." Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, your Hotel Palace, if I remember, it has got a nice cafeteria out front? In the summer, there are umbrellas and you can have a nectar, pivo; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if I go in there and say to the waiter I want a nectar and a kisela minerale, he's going to bring me a beer and a mineral water. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Because that means in addition to, it means one and another plus something else. Right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you should lead the witness straight to the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to avoid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you're getting him confused. He's a little bit baffled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So your order is pursuant to the decision we've just looked at and, in addition to that, your assessment of the situation on the ground in the Autonomous Region of Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that goes back to what we talked about, explanation subparagraph 3 of Subotic's order saying "take a look at the situation in your territory and take appropriate action." Right? We just talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the additions you've made, Mr. Cunningham pointed out yesterday that there is this decision that disarmament will take place by 1500 hours on 11 of May. That's number 5. But you've also -- what has also been added to this decision, number 4, is the curfew; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And at the very end, you've pointed out in number 4 that the presidents of the councils for National Defence shall be held responsible for the implementing of this decision. They shall therefore be given full authority for the purposes of carrying out the decision. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, it's called a decision, but this is mandatory, isn't it? This is the same as an order. This has to be carried out. You're sending this out as secretary of the Secretariat for Defence.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at P166, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's not in the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, take a moment and look at that, sir. This is the Banja Luka CSB dispatch of the 4th of May 1992. It's to the chiefs of all public security stations. It states: "We have received a dispatch from the Government of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina in Banja Luka, which we hereby forward to you in full." And what follows verbatim is your decision we just talked about of the 4th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So we know that on the same day or very close to the same day as you made your decision, it was sent to all the police stations in the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at the bottom, underneath where your order ends, there's -- a -- additional writing from Stojan Zupljanin. "With regard to the above-mentioned, it is necessary that you immediately and without delay undertake the necessary activities described in the above decision and report to us about this as well as about all events of interest for the security situation ..." And it goes on to talk about the curfew and says that the chiefs of the public security stations are personally responsible for the implementation of this decision. So this is one of those pretty clear, precise orders from Mr. Zupljanin that I was talking about -- we were talking about right at the beginning of your cross-examination; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at P1190, please. And I'll tell you, sir, I'm not going to surprise you at all; I'm going to show where your order went and how it was acted upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We have a revised translation, Your Honour, that's not on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How far is it going to complicate our lives? That's what I want to know, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think it's going to matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's not going to matter, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can scroll down. No, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, here we are the next day, the 5th of May, at the National Defence Council meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, headed by its president, Dr. Milomir Stakic. Conclusion 2. Can you look at that, please, sir. "Mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region Assembly are to be carried out when the actual situation in the municipality renders it necessary, in accordance with requirements and a special plan, through call-up papers issued by the municipal secretariat for national defence." And if you go to number 7, it's right towards the end of the document: "All paramilitary formations and individuals who possess weapons and ammunition illegally are called upon to surrender them immediately and not later than 11 May 1992 at 1500 hours" at the police station - I'm paraphrasing. After this period, the relevant organs will start searches and seizures of any such weapons and ammunition and will apply the most rigorous sanctions. So here, we can see that your order was, in fact, sent to Prijedor and was discussed at the National Defence Council meeting, and conclusions were made based on it. And by "your order," I'm just talking about that document from the 4th of May which Mr. Zupljanin sent out; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the subject, yes. But if I may be allowed to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mobilisation had been ordered by the defence minister and then passed with an addendum which we see here, which was signed by me, the Secretary of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. The essence was to mobilise units, and as for my assessment, to disarm paramilitary individuals and so on and so forth. This is not an order by the Assembly of the ARK or by an official body or executive council of the ARK. This was for the command, and the Security Services Centre also took place in it because they saw their own duties and tasks involved in terms of collecting weapons, presumably, and the curfew. This document that I see in front of me, in the conclusions Milomir Stakic says the following: This is not a decision of the Assembly of Bosanska Krajina; this is a decision of the defence minister which I later postponed. This is proof that in a confused situation, people drew different conclusions and based their decisions on a number of different conclusions. This order should first and foremost have been carried out with no further ado to begin with. Thank you very much for allowing me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And obviously, rather than Bogdan Subotic sending this order, his order directly to Prijedor, he sent it out; and as you say, additions were made, including the curfew, the disarmament provisions, and it's then sent to Prijedor; right? You nodded. You need to answer verbally.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And apparently we can see here that the addition about disarmament was accepted and was going to be acted upon right away, as you said it should have been; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you P180, sir. You can have my copy if Denise can get me another one. This is the article from Oslobodenje from 9th of May 1992. We've already talked about the chain of ARK Crisis Staff disarmament conclusions from 8th and 9th May. Take a look at that, sir. It's the -- there's a lot on your page in B/C/S, but I'm interested in the one with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the headline "Weapons must be returned." It's a short article. It states: "Banja Luka, 8th May. Members of paramilitary units and individuals from the area of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina must return all weapons and other means of combat in their illegal possession by 11 May. Stated today, Radoslav Brdjanin, the commander of the war staff of Bosanska Krajina." And then Mr. Brdjanin continues to talk about the mobilisation being consistently implemented and some other issues. That's what it says in your copy; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You can make your comment in a minute. I'm just trying to make it clear now that we're both reading the same words. Now, Mr. Brdjanin, as president of the ARK Crisis Staff, he's going out in the media and letting everybody know about this weapons deadline under his capacity, it says here, as commander of the war staff. Right? That's what he's doing; he's making sure that that deadline issued in the May 4th order, passed down through Mr. Zupljanin to the CSBs, discussed in Prijedor, is also being broadcast through the print media.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I answer this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I can make it much shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin in his capacity as president of the ARK Crisis Staff is emphasising in the media the importance that these weapons need to be returned by the 11 May deadline. Right? That's what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you have your comment -- we're going to take a break soon, but if you have a comment you feel you need to make, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General mobilisation had been declared. When I say "general," this means that it could be announced in any way at all. In this case, it was an order. Whoever declares general mobilisation, there's no mistake, no error involved. It's just that war staff, crisis staff, these two concepts are being confused here in the media. Are we talking about a war staff or a crisis staff? Because it is my submission that these are two different concepts and two different bodies. But I don't have to comment on that. So whoever could appear, whoever could insist that the order be carried out, this would indeed have been very beneficial for the order to be carried out because the purpose of the order was to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, I've lost track of the breaking schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We started at 7 minutes past 4.00, but we could actually start our break here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How late are we going, Your Honour? I have been asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My intention was to go right up to 7.00. But it depends. How much longer do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd hate to guess right now. I won't finish today. If we take the break now, I can see ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Usher, could you please escort the witness out. We are going to have another break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of the sixth amended indictment, you still specifically retain mention of the three municipalities, Bihac, Ripac, and Bosanska Dubica and Bosanska Krupa. It wouldn't itself be a problem to us because it's neither hot nor cold, but then there are several other paragraphs throughout the indictment that impute a crime to the accused, specifically referring to that crime being committed in the municipalities mentioned in paragraph 4. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason it was left in is because paragraph 4 is -- was a description of the autonomous region, and we're told by Mr. Ackerman that he's going to be calling evidence from Dubica and Gradiska. And there's no doubt about it. That's the case, although we dropped it, we're going to be imputing crimes that were committed in Gradiska and Dubica to Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- anyway, have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I made it very clear that I'm not calling witnesses from any of those places.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you said Laktasi and Srbac, and not Dubica and Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's break now. We'll have, if you agree, a 20-minute break, and then try and finish a little bit earlier, I'm told. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. This will be quite quick. I want to show you another news article from the same day. This time it's from the newspaper Glas. I have a copy here. I'm interested in the story entitled "No more time to beat around the bush." Subject: "Report from the session of the Krajina war staff, Banja Luka, 8th of May." This is a report on one of those ARK Crisis Staff meetings which we ran through earlier. It states: "At today's session of the ARK war staff, the implementation of previous decisions of this body was analysed, specifically the success of the mobilisation of recruits and measures taken to prevent men liable for military service from leaving the area." So again, it's reporting on discussions of the security situation as they have been addressed in the ARK Crisis Staff. "Significant attention was also paid to implementation of the war staff's order on disarming illegal formations and individuals who obtained weapons through various channels." That's the first paragraph. If you skip to the third: "Speaking about the order to disarm individuals and illegal formations, Brdjanin warned that he expected most of them to return their weapons to the municipal staffs of the TO by 11 May, adding that weapons would be taken by force from those who refused to do so." So again, you've explained to us how you see a different between a war staff and a crisis staff. I don't want to talk about that now. What we have here is Mr. Brdjanin in his capacity as president of the ARK Crisis Staff in its early days portraying to the public this decision as a decision taken by his staff; right? Specifically, that weapons must be surrendered by the 11th of May. You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So in public, the crisis staff is throwing its weight behind that deadline emphasising this is an important deadline, if it's not met, these weapons are going to be taken by force.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was provided for by the order of mobilisation. If weapons weren't surrendered, that's how it would be. That's the situation today, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What do you mean by "that's the situation today, too"? That's what I didn't understand when you said that before either.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone who has possession of illegal arms and were not in a unit and was not issued weapons which was required by the order, the -- it was necessary to return the weapons. That part of the decision was carried out by the civilian bodies of the police. In cases of uniforms, it was the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand it is always illegal to own an illegal weapon, however that's defined in the law. Here, though, we're talking about the specific deadline in the order which you'll agree with me Mr. Brdjanin here is portraying that as an ARK Crisis Staff order; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has already answered that question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, he has, Your Honour, it's just that he's starting to talk about the current law, and I'm differentiating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, there are other documents - I'm trying to speed this up - would you agree with me or accept that there were public announcements in Kljuc about the deadline of the 11th of May, issued by the Kljuc Municipal Crisis Staff? Otherwise, we can look at some documents.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so. I didn't look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. You assume that because that would be natural. This order has been issued, it has been disseminated, and Kljuc Crisis Staff would be one of the bodies that would publicise that deadline; right? I can show it to you if you want to see it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, you don't want to see it, or no, you disagree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need for me to see it, but you can show it to me if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's all right. I'd like to now show you P202. This is a lengthy dispatch sent out by chief of the security centre, Stoja Zupljanin. I don't want you to get confused because there are several dates on this document. It's the conclusions of the 6th of May expanded meeting, but the document has dispatched on the 20th of May. As you can see, just take a look at the top of the document, these conclusions have been sent to all SJBs, every police station in the region, except for Jajce. Now, quickly, could you just go to paragraph 23. Read that to yourself. Let me know when you've read it. It states that "In all our activities, we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region. "With regard to disarmament, when the deadline for weapons surrender expires on 11 May 1992, on 11 May 1992, we should take no action until the Crisis Staff makes the relevant decisions. It is very important that we solve this problem comprehensively, insisting on the disarmament of extremist groups." Have you read that, sir? So, it's not just Mr. Brdjanin in the press; Stojan Zupljanin in this precise order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Taya is right. We do not have -- I did hear the witness answering the question, but probably did not arrive to the interpreters. You were asked whether you read this document, and you answered yes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What perhaps could be clarified is whether he mean having read it now or whether you meant to ask him if he had read it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I actually meant, sir, have you just finished reading this paragraph just now because before I ask you any questions I want to make sure you've had time to read it. So you've read it just now these last few minutes; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you ever read this document before today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You weren't shown this one by Defence counsel in preparing for today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. It's not important. The question to you, sir, is it's not just in the newspapers, it's just not Mr. Brdjanin; Stojan Zupljanin in this order, which is sent to every police station in the region, is first of all saying that in all activities, the police are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the ARK. Right? That's what he's saying. It's unambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the second point he makes specifically to the issue of the disarmament deadline because when that deadline is reached and expires, no action is going to be taken until the crisis staff makes the relevant decision; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So -- we'll get back to this, but whoever discussed that deadline when you first put it in your order at this point, early May, it's very clear that the crisis staff is controlling what's going to happen when that deadline expires, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just ask you this without showing you the document. I don't think you need to see it. I'm done with that, sir. You already told us you were at the 16th assembly session on the 12th of May. That was the day after the first deadline; right? The deadline was the 11th of May; the assembly was on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember Miroslav Vjestica from Krupa reporting what was happening in the assembly to neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Miroslav Vjestica at the assembly, but I don't remember what he was reporting on. I got to know Mr. Miroslav as an assemblyman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read you a part of what he said, and you tell me if that helps you remember or not. He states: "As for Bosanski Novi, let me you that I was there yesterday." -- which would be the 11th of May -- "Bosanski Novi is sealed off. On ultimatum has been issued and a deadline set for the Muslims to surrender their weapons. Some of them; some of them have not. Yesterday, there was shooting. What will happen today, I believe they will surrender. The same is going on in Sanski Most. I think that the Muslims will be disarmed there, too." I can show you the transcript if you want, or can you agree with me that he said that at the 16th assembly session?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having him say that. Perhaps I wasn't present at that point in time. I didn't attend the whole assembly. I was there at the beginning. Then there was a break when I was standing with three high-ranking officers. And later on, I came back to the meeting, and I listened to the report of the commander of the Main Staff. But I can't remember that particular discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. That's fine. Let me just show it to you very quickly so you can tell I'm being truthful with you. It's the highlighted portion in yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'm looking at P50, Your Honours, page 26 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Very simply, Mr. Vjestica there is talking about results of the 11th of May deadline in Novi; right? It's quite clear, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm done with that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you P631, sir. I have it here if it helps. Now, this is pretty simple, too. This is a report from the 5th Corps Command signed for General Talic on the 12th of May, the day his command was going to turn into the 1KK, to the 2nd Military District. Section 3 is entitled "Situation on the Ground." That's the only part I'm going to ask you about. And it states: "Upon the request of citizens and parties, the SR Krajina war staff has extended the deadline for the handover of weapons from 11 of May to 14th of May." Have you found that part? It's the bottom of number 3.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, just very simply, this is just a report from General Talic up through the chain of command that we talked about earlier reporting on the ARK Crisis Staff conclusion which we saw earlier today about the extension of the deadline.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's probably something he would have learned from, I think it's Major Vunovic who attended the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that. That calls for speculation on his part how he would have found out about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not speculation at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is speculation, Mr. Nicholls. Please withdraw your --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My I just give my foundation. On direct, Mr. Cunningham led out of the witness I believe that General Talic, when he couldn't attend sent a representative to inform him. And he said that that representative, he believed, did not take part but took notes or recorded what was said so he could brief his superior. So I think that's a foundation to ask if that's how it's likely that he would have found out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, you are right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You can answer the question. That's probably how General Talic found out, or that's why Major Vunovic was there, to convey this kind of information to General Talic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Which major?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, General Talic couldn't attend -- I don't want to spend a lot of time on this point - you said he sent Vunovic. There was a representative for the 5th Corps at ARK Crisis Staff meetings; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Gojko Vujinovic. I don't remember him being at the crisis staff, but at the meetings of the presidents of the municipality. That is what I said, and his name is Gojko Vujinovic. And Major Jokic was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not asking about Major Jokic. It's okay. I'll just move on; it's not vital how that information reached him. Now, we also talked about, and you agreed with me, that the way these weapons disarmament operations were going to take place properly was at the hands of the police and the military police; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we've seen that in Mr. Zupljanin's order. I'd like to show you P637. And while you're getting that, let me ask you if you personally knew Colonel Anicic, who was the Serbian TO commander for Sanski Most in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What you're looking at is a 22nd of May Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most, "Set of Conclusions" from their 21st of May meeting. I'd like you to look at item 4, please. That's number 4, not necessarily -- not D, but number 4. It states: "As far as disarming paramilitary formations in Sanski Most is concerned, Colonel Basara and Colonel Anicic are charged with putting this into practice." And then it states that in Sanski Most, there is now a deadline of 2000 hours on 24th of May 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, do you know who Colonel Basara was? You know who he is, right? Branko Basara.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade commander, one of the brigades in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. So here what we're seeing is that the disarming in Sanski Most is not exclusively being handled by the police and the military police, but also with the TO represented by Colonel Anicic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The TO did not have its own police establishment-wise. Whether Anicic maybe set up his own police or not, I don't know. Maybe he did. But there was a rule. There were two kinds of police: The military police at the disposal of the corps, and the civilian police. This was according to the rules. Colonel Anicic did not have the same TO that I had, and I did not have the military police. I'm not sure if that answers your question. But this seems more like --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're -- you're --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- like some kind of initiative on Anicic's part. But all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's a conclusion directed to Colonel Anicic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me -- this might help clear this up for you. Let me show you P638. I have a copy here. This shows you, as you can see, that Nedeljko Anicic was, of course, Serbian TO commander; right? You can see that in the top left of the cover page.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, the combat task is disarmament operations in Sanski Most. Do you see that, right at the top of the page? That's what it says the order is about.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this is an order. The authorising commander, probably the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm losing my ... Okay, the sound's back, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem? I haven't understood what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't get any sound from that last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you follow from the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, it's fine. It's back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, the sound is back. Okay, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Very quickly, if you look down to number 3 of this rather long, detailed order, it states: "The 6th Brigade in coordinated action with Serbian TO units is undertaking combat operations in Sanski Most Municipality area in order to disarm enemy forces ..." Again, so based on the specific situation in Sanski Most, keeping in mind that we are now beyond the 11th and 14th of May deadlines, disarmament operations are taking place -- being conducted by a regular VRS unit in conjunction with the TO; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3, the neighbours, that's the 6th Brigade. That's what the order says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, right. I'm just trying to go through with you the evolution of how these orders which we've talked about being passed down were put into place. Thank you, I'm done with that. I'd like to show you P196. Again, you can have my copy if that's easier. Sir, these are Kljuc Crisis Staff minutes from the 13th and 14th of May. So now just after the first deadline and right up to when the second deadline expired. Agenda item number 1 is "adoption of decisions, conclusions on behalf of the Kljuc SO pursuant to decisions of the Krajina ARK Crisis Staffs." And if you go down from the agenda which has been discussed, to conclusion number 1, again, the deadline for the surrender of illegally acquired weapons will be extended until 2400 hours on the 14th of May 1992. And if you continue: "Once the deadline has expired, officers of the Security Services Centre of the Krajina Autonomous Region will proceed to confiscate weapons and take strict measures against those who fail to respond to the call of the Crisis Staff." Point 4, just below that, it states: "This meeting supports the activities of the Krajina Autonomous Region Crisis Staff." You said that not all conclusions or decisions were implemented in all municipalities. Here, we see Kljuc Crisis Staff recognising the authority of the ARK Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I comment, please, or should I just answer yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You could answer yes or no, and then comment. That would be best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And when Mr. Nicholls gives you permission, it's also our permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If someone is a superior and if the Kljuc Crisis Staff believed that the ARK Crisis Staff was their superior, there is nothing for me to confirm here. I do agree that if you look at the sentence, you might conclude that at the same time as it supported the ARK Crisis Staff, maybe they didn't believe that they were their superiors. But yes, I would take that to be a yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. And we can move on from this. One of the conclusions they're definitely implementing here is the weapons deadline of 14 May. That was conclusions item number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I get an idea of when you plan on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Five minutes, five minutes more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. If it's five minutes more, Your Honour, I'd just as soon break now. And I will try to organise things to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough. We have all had a very long day. And it's not finished yet. So Mr. Sajic, we are going to end here today. We will continue tomorrow. Tomorrow, the sitting is also in the afternoon, so you will have ample time to rest, and we hope to be able to finish -- I think the indication is that we should be in a position to finish with your testimony tomorrow for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Definitely. From our side, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then in the beginning, Mr. Cunningham, please give us an indication as to how much time you require for any redirect that you might require.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'll be glad to do that, Your Honour. And if I could ask Mr. Nicholls just how much time he thinks he's going to use up because we have a witness that we can put on tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to read the transcript and try to reformulate. And I think I'll finish in the first session, the first hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And the other witness that you have in line, that you're proofing tomorrow, he is listed or she is indicated as being required here to today for a day and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think, and I apologise for interrupting, Your Honour. I think, I haven't met with him to proof him yet, but I'm thinking that my direct examination or my examination-in-chief would be stretching it if it was 45 minutes long. So I anticipate it being, relatively, a very brief examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not my witness, so I can't speak to the cross. But I think reading the summary of the municipality that witness is from, we will be longer than 45 minutes on cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When I read the summary, I just couldn't fathom how this witness would be a day and a half. But anyway, it's up to you. We'll come to that tomorrow. And tomorrow we'll decide what to do. Mr. Sajic, you're free to go. Usher will escort you out of the courtroom and we'll see you again tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask you something, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said yesterday that I shouldn't use the phone to talk to anyone, so I simply switched it off after my conversation with the Defence team. I still keep it switched off. But I need to check on my mother, on her health. May I turn my phone back on to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, certainly. Without the least hesitation. You are a mature man, so you know what's good and what's bad, what's right and what's wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So speaking to your mother or checking that your mother is all right is an honourable thing to do. You should not even doubt that we would ever put you in a position prohibiting you or making it impossible for you to check on your mother's health. I check myself on a daily basis with regard to my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If he asks how it's all going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if she asks you what has the others said about you, please be careful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I'll bring that up. I just want to get in touch to see how she is. The people from the Victims and Witnesses Unit have been very kind to me so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they will continue to be kind, nice to you because that's the practice in this Tribunal. We don't distinguish between witnesses coming for the Prosecution or witnesses for the Defence. They are all treated the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything before we rise? Mr. Nicholls? Mr. Ackerman? Mr. Cunningham? Are you feeling well, Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm better, Your Honour. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we rise, and we'll meet again tomorrow in the afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of December, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.45 p.m.,
